newsitem.title: CHINA: Press Digest - HK Newspaper Headlines - Aug 4.
newsitem.headline: Press Digest - HK Newspaper Headlines - Aug 4.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- Legislator David Chu wrote to the Chinese University suggesting an academic who had criticised him should be sacked. Chu also wrote to another university to condemn an academic who found fault with him.

-- China's Post and Telecommunications Minister Wu Jichuan said the China Telecom (HK) listing was a capital-raising exercise and would not give foreign investors a controlling say in the China mainland market.

-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- Critics said the outcome of a legal challenge to the Provisional Legislature had exposed "a major flaw' in China's constitution. Lawyer Albert Ho said the ruling showed there was no mechanism for aggrieved parties to overturn decisions by the National People's Congress in courts.
-- EXPRESS NEWS -- Owners of major entertainment nightspots said Hong Kong people's lifestyle had not changed after the handover, and their business was unaffected.
-- WEN WEI PO -- To accelerate reforms of its cadre system, Beijing has sent people to cities and provinces to investigate the personnel system. The work was to be finished in mid-August.

-- Experts said Cantonese eating habits might cause cancer of the esophagus, which was more commonly found in Guangdong province than elsewhere. Experts said Cantonese food stressed variety, but did not pay attention to its effects on health.
-- MING PAO -- Beijing launched a propaganda campaign on Sunday to prepare for the 15th Communist Party Congress.

-- ECONOMIC JOURNAL -- New World Infrastructure and Cosco Hong Kong have decided to become strategic investors in the Sichuan Chengdu Highway Limited, holding a total of 9.96 per cent stake in the company.
